question: WHY do actual canvas clicks now fail pointer lock, whereas the 15:17/15:24 manual-focused witness/input captures on the same app/source succeeded?
answerOneLine: The premise did not reproduce: ONE ordinary real canvas click took pointer lock on the FIRST attempt at 16:40:59Z on the SAME source (dc63fba...), SAME preview 38007 (index 1f699b4a, bundle 4f39f1ea), SAME URL, SAME headed GB10 ANGLE recipe, 9 minutes after the 16:31 failure. The 16:31 refusal is therefore NOT a deterministic property of this build/entry, and its cause remains UNPROVED.
verdict: POINTER-LOCK-SUCCEEDED — entry input path (click->lock->keyboard) works under current conditions; prior browser/OS cause NOT confirmed and NOT reproduced
provedFacts: Real click at canvas centre (640,360) -> document.pointerLockElement === canvas after 15 ms; 1 pointerlockchange, 0 pointerlockerror, 0 authored 'Pointer lock request failed:' console.warn.

Because the lock was granted, the authored CameraControls handleClick necessarily passed ALL THREE of its clauses (target===canvas, no lock held, allowsMousePointerLock true) and element.requestPointerLock() resolved. No early return, no rejection.

Touch facts measured for the first time (never observed by the prior report): navigator.maxTouchPoints=0, 'ontouchstart' in window=false, innerWidth=1280, matchMedia(pointer:coarse)=false / (pointer:fine)=true / (hover:none)=false; isTouchDevice() recomputed from the same facts = FALSE; NO shipped touch-controls DOM mounted (touch-joystick absent, touch-action-cluster absent, zero data-testid starting 'touch-'). Therefore mobileInput touchActive was false and the touchActive clause of allowsMousePointerLock cannot have caused a refusal in this environment configuration.

Pre-click state matched the 16:31 record exactly: hasFocus true, visibilityState visible, activeElement body, pointerLockElement null, elementFromPoint(centre) IS the canvas with pointerEvents auto, worldBound true, settled spread 0.0022u, supported true, policy moveSpeedScale 1 / lookMode free, movie flag null, autopilot absent.

Keyboard path is independently enabled: one ordinary 100 ms W pulse (DIAGNOSTIC ONLY) moved the body from z -5.999999998 to z -6.513055322, displacement 0.513055324 u (non-zero, measured, not inferred); key released; pointer lock held at the pulse.
navigator.userActivation at the click: isActive true, hasBeenActive true.
correctionsToTheCommonManualRuntimeRepor: 'allowsMousePointerLock passed' was an ASSERTION, not a measurement: the 16:31 probe never observed click pointerType, sourceCapabilities.firesTouchEvents, or touchActive/touch-controls DOM. This diagnostic measured those facts (all mouse-compatible, no touch UI) but only for the 16:40 session; they cannot be back-applied to 16:31.

'the refusal came from the browser/OS layer' is NOT established. The 16:31 probe captured no page console, no pointerlockerror event and no native rejection reason, and OS-level window activation was never measured. The same recipe now passes, so a persistent browser/OS refusal is contradicted as a standing condition.
document.hasFocus()===true does NOT rule out loss of OS-level window activation; the report's rulesOut list did not eliminate that candidate.
unknownsNotMeasured: The exact per-click pointerType / sourceCapabilities / isTrusted fields were NOT captured in this session: BOTH read-only observer listeners threw TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')" at click time (2 pageerrors at 16:40:59.153/.155) because this probe's own describe() helper called tagName.toLowerCase() on event.currentTarget, which is window/document. This is a defect in THIS probe's bookkeeping only; it did not touch the game handler (the lock was granted in the same click).

What differed at 16:31:26-16:31:38 is unmeasured and is now unrecoverable: that session captured no console, no pointerlockerror, no native reason, no OS window-activation state, and it has been cleaned up.
Foreign window/X11 input-focus ownership at either time was not inspected (out of scope by commission).

A shader-warmup warning ('initial render released without complete preparation', outcome timeout, elapsedMs 3926) was present in THIS run; whether it was present at 16:31 is unknown because that console was never captured.
causeIfProved: NOT PROVED. Proved only that under current conditions the shipped entry-input path (real click -> authored handleClick -> requestPointerLock -> lock -> keyboard movement) works end to end. The 16:31 failure is non-reproducible with the identical recipe and its cause stays open; OS blame is NOT supported by any measurement.
minimalNextAction: Do NOT accept 'browser/OS pointer-lock refusal' as a standing blocker: it did not reproduce.

Before any re-commissioned manual COMMON run, the SHARED probe (owned by another role; not edited here) needs three read-only additions inside its existing pointer-lock loop: page console capture, a document 'pointerlockerror' listener, and the click-event fields (isTrusted/pointerType/sourceCapabilities). Then a refusal records its own native reason instead of being inferred.
One-line fix to THIS owned probe before any reuse: describe() must guard non-Element targets (currentTarget window/document) so the click observer cannot throw.
No further manual retry loop is warranted from this role.
notAcceptance: This diagnostic is NOT manual playability, NOT a COMMON passage, NOT a defect closure, NOT chapter approval and NOT a new workflow. The W pulse was diagnostic instrumentation of the keyboard path only; no chapter progress was sought or made. No game state was written.
